newsitem.title: GERMANY: IG Metall says prepared to talk more on sick pay.
newsitem.headline: IG Metall says prepared to talk more on sick pay.

text.p: Klaus Zwickel, head of the German engineering union IG Metall, said on Thursday his union remained open to talks with engineering employers on sick pay and other pay issues.
But he was pessimistic about the likelhood of a near-term resolution to the dispute. "There are absolutely no grounds for optimism," he said.

The union is protesting against employer plans to implement a new law that allows employers to reduce sick pay to 80 percent of the normal wage from 100 percent. The unions have rejected this as an attack on their bargaining rights.
No progress was made toward resolving the issue in four hours of talks between the two sides today.
Zwickel said the union was hoping to resume talks with the employers on October 21.
On entering the talks, he threatened a day of industrial action on October 24 if no progress was made by October 23. --Frankfurt Newsroom +49 69 756525
